story: Brooke Gile was first author of a small 2026 pilot study of low-dose rapamycin in people with ME/CFS, a long-term illness marked by severe fatigue. There was no placebo group. Patients who responded to rapamycin showed shifts in purine chemicals in their blood, consistent with lower activity of the enzyme IMP dehydrogenase in blood cells. Lab tests suggested that such purine changes can harm mitochondria and feed inflammation in microglia, but those links were not measured in the patients. PubMed lists Gile at Simmaron Research.

highlights.GIL2026: First author of the pilot study linking rapamycin treatment in ME/CFS to reduced fatigue and changed purine levels.

Roy A.lab_name: Milwaukee Institute for Drug Discovery, University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee (Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA)
Roy A.role: Senior (last) author of a 2026 phase-II pilot study of low-dose rapamycin in people with ME/CFS.
Roy A.sub: Simmaron Research · Milwaukee Institute for Drug Discovery, University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee, USA
story: Avik Roy was last author of a 2026 pilot study in which people with ME/CFS took low-dose rapamycin. It was an uncontrolled study with no placebo, and fatigue went down. In patients who responded, purine chemicals in the blood shifted in a way that fits lower IMP dehydrogenase activity. Lab experiments suggested that altered purines can impair mitochondria and promote microglial inflammation, but this was not tested in the patients. PubMed lists Roy at Simmaron Research and at the Milwaukee Institute for Drug Discovery.

highlights.GIL2026: Last author of the pilot study linking rapamycin treatment in ME/CFS to reduced fatigue and changed purine levels.

Zong Y.lab_name: Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine, University of Wisconsin-Madison (Madison, Wisconsin, USA)
Zong Y.role: Senior (last) author of a 2026 study on GPR143 as a tissue marker for kidney tumors with FLCN, TSC or MTOR changes.
Zong Y.sub: Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine, University of Wisconsin-Madison, USA
story: Yang Zong was last author of a 2026 pathology study that looked for a better test to spot certain kidney tumors. These tumors carry changes in the FLCN, TSC or MTOR genes or in TFE transcription factors. The team found that the protein GPR143 shows up in staining of these tumors and can work alongside the existing marker GPNMB. This was a tissue and database study, not a treatment trial. PubMed lists Zong at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

highlights.LI2026: Last author of the study proposing GPR143 staining as a diagnostic marker for kidney tumors with FLCN/TSC/MTOR-TFE alterations.

Ouyang G.lab_name: Division of Hepatobiliary Surgery, The First Affiliated Hospital of Guangxi Medical University (Nanning, China)
Ouyang G.role: Senior (last) author of a 2026 mouse study on notoginsenoside R1 and acetaminophen-induced liver injury.
Ouyang G.sub: Division of Hepatobiliary Surgery, First Affiliated Hospital of Guangxi Medical University, Nanning, China
story: Guoqing Ouyang was last author of a 2026 study in mice on liver damage from an acetaminophen overdose. The compound notoginsenoside R1 reduced the damage by calming the MAPK/mTOR pathway and restoring protective autophagy, which cuts liver cell death and oxidative harm. The work was done in mice and cells. PubMed lists Ouyang at the First Affiliated Hospital of Guangxi Medical University in Nanning.

highlights.LIS2026: Last author of the study showing that notoginsenoside R1 protects the liver through MAPK/mTOR-controlled autophagy.

Lv N.lab_name: School of Medicine, Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine (Nanjing, China)
Lv N.role: First author of a 2026 mouse study on Lamtor5 loss, macrophage ageing and systemic ageing.
Lv N.sub: School of Medicine, Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine, China · Institute of Translational Medicine, Zhejiang Shuren University, China
story: Nianyin Lv was first author of a 2026 mouse study on how the immune system ages. Lamtor5 is a subunit of a lysosomal complex that activates mTOR. The study found that its levels fall with age, and that losing it makes macrophages (immune cells) senescent. Those cells release signals through cGAS-STING that drive inflammation and ageing features in the whole animal. Putting Lamtor5 back in aged mice reduced these signs. PubMed lists Lv at Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine and at Zhejiang Shuren University.

highlights.LV2026: First author of the study linking falling Lamtor5 to macrophage senescence and ageing in mice.

Shi L.lab_name: Institute of Translational Medicine, Zhejiang Shuren University (Hangzhou, China)
Shi L.role: Senior (last) author of a 2026 mouse study on Lamtor5 loss, macrophage ageing and systemic ageing.
Shi L.sub: Institute of Translational Medicine, Zhejiang Shuren University · Yuhang Institute of Medical Science Innovation and Transformation, Hangzhou, China
story: Liyun Shi was last author of a 2026 mouse study on immune ageing. The work showed that the mTOR-activating protein Lamtor5 declines with age and that its loss pushes macrophages into senescence and sets off cGAS-STING inflammation that spreads to other tissues. Restoring Lamtor5 in old mice eased these ageing signs. PubMed lists Shi at the Institute of Translational Medicine, Zhejiang Shuren University in Hangzhou.

highlights.LV2026: Last author of the study linking falling Lamtor5 to macrophage senescence and ageing in mice.

Martins-Branco D.lab_name: Institut Jules Bordet, Université libre de Bruxelles (Brussels, Belgium)
Martins-Branco D.role: First author of the 2026 EVERGREEN study of everolimus after CDK4/6 inhibitor treatment in advanced breast cancer.
Martins-Branco D.sub: Institut Jules Bordet, Université libre de Bruxelles, Belgium
story: Diogo Martins-Branco was first author of EVERGREEN, a 2026 multicentre study of women with ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer whose disease had progressed on a CDK4/6 inhibitor. Adding everolimus (an mTOR inhibitor) to hormone therapy gave a modest gain in progression-free survival, 5.0 versus 4.3 months, with no clear gain in overall survival. The study was retrospective and not randomised, so treatment-selection bias cannot be ruled out. PubMed lists Martins-Branco at the Institut Jules Bordet in Brussels.

highlights.MAR2026: First author of the EVERGREEN study of everolimus plus hormone therapy after CDK4/6 inhibitor progression.

de Azambuja E.lab_name: Institut Jules Bordet, Université libre de Bruxelles (Brussels, Belgium)
de Azambuja E.role: Senior (last) author of the 2026 EVERGREEN study of everolimus after CDK4/6 inhibitor treatment in advanced breast cancer.
de Azambuja E.sub: Institut Jules Bordet, Université libre de Bruxelles, Belgium
story: Evandro de Azambuja was last author of EVERGREEN, a 2026 multicentre study in women with ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer that had progressed on a CDK4/6 inhibitor. Adding the mTOR inhibitor everolimus to hormone therapy gave a modest gain in progression-free survival, 5.0 versus 4.3 months, and no clear gain in overall survival. Because the study was retrospective and not randomised, selection bias is possible. PubMed lists de Azambuja at the Institut Jules Bordet in Brussels.

highlights.MAR2026: Last author of the EVERGREEN study of everolimus plus hormone therapy after CDK4/6 inhibitor progression.

Bo S.lab_name: Department of Cardiothoracic Surgery, Xiangyang No.1 People's Hospital (Xiangyang, China)
Bo S.role: First author of a 2026 computer and cell-culture study of gambogic acid in lung cancer cells.
Bo S.sub: Department of Cardiothoracic Surgery, Xiangyang No.1 People's Hospital, China
story: Su Bo was first author of a 2026 study that combined computer modelling with lab work on lung cancer cells. Gambogic acid, a natural compound, killed A549 lung cancer cells and triggered cell death. In the docking analysis it bound most tightly to AKT and to S6K1, a target downstream of mTOR. The study did not measure direct inhibition of the mTOR kinase and had no animal or human data. PubMed lists Bo at Xiangyang No.1 People's Hospital.

highlights.BO2026: First author of the study testing gambogic acid in lung cancer cells and docking it to AKT and S6K1.

Dąbkowska A.lab_name: Department of Immunology, Mossakowski Medical Research Institute, Polish Academy of Sciences (Warsaw, Poland)
Dąbkowska A.role: First author of a 2026 study showing that mTORC1 inhibitors raise CD20 in B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
Dąbkowska A.sub: Department of Immunology, Mossakowski Medical Research Institute, Polish Academy of Sciences, Warsaw, Poland
story: Agnieszka Dąbkowska was first author of a 2026 leukemia study. The team found that mTORC1 inhibitors raise the amount of CD20 on B-cell precursor ALL cells through the AKT-FOXO1 route and push the cells toward a more mature state. This made anti-CD20 antibody drugs work better, including in high-risk disease with IKZF1 deletions. The work used cell lines and mouse models. PubMed lists Dąbkowska at the Mossakowski Medical Research Institute in Warsaw.

highlights.DAB2026: First author of the study showing that mTORC1 inhibition boosts CD20 and anti-CD20 antibody effect in B-cell precursor ALL.

Firczuk M.lab_name: Department of Immunology, Mossakowski Medical Research Institute, Polish Academy of Sciences (Warsaw, Poland)
Firczuk M.role: Senior (last) author of a 2026 study showing that mTORC1 inhibitors raise CD20 in B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
Firczuk M.sub: Department of Immunology, Mossakowski Medical Research Institute, Polish Academy of Sciences, Warsaw, Poland
story: Malgorzata Firczuk was last author of a 2026 leukemia study. It showed that mTORC1 inhibitors increase CD20 on B-cell precursor ALL cells via the AKT-FOXO1 axis and promote B-cell maturation, which made anti-CD20 antibodies more effective, also in high-risk IKZF1-deleted disease. The evidence comes from cell lines and mice, and it gives a reason to test the combination in patients. PubMed lists Firczuk at the Mossakowski Medical Research Institute in Warsaw.

highlights.DAB2026: Last author of the study showing that mTORC1 inhibition boosts CD20 and anti-CD20 antibody effect in B-cell precursor ALL.

Deniz O.lab_name: Faculty of Biological and Environmental Sciences, University of Helsinki (Helsinki, Finland)
Deniz O.role: First author of a 2026 Drosophila study identifying Spalt-related as an mTORC1 inhibitor driven by the integrated stress response.
Deniz O.sub: Faculty of Biological and Environmental Sciences & Institute of Biotechnology, University of Helsinki, Finland
story: Onur Deniz was first author of a 2026 study in fruit flies. The team found that the transcription factor Spalt-related (Salr) holds back mTORC1-driven growth and fat storage in the fat body when nutrients are scarce. Salr is switched on slowly by the integrated stress response, and it works alongside FoxO rather than downstream of it. PubMed lists Deniz at the University of Helsinki.

highlights.DEN2026: First author of the study identifying Salr as an integrated-stress-response-driven brake on mTORC1 growth in Drosophila.

Hietakangas V.lab_name: Faculty of Biological and Environmental Sciences, University of Helsinki (Helsinki, Finland)
Hietakangas V.role: Senior (last) author of a 2026 Drosophila study identifying Spalt-related as an mTORC1 inhibitor driven by the integrated stress response.
Hietakangas V.sub: Faculty of Biological and Environmental Sciences & Institute of Biotechnology, University of Helsinki, Finland
story: Ville Hietakangas was last author of a 2026 study in fruit flies on how cells slow growth when food runs short. The work identified the transcription factor Spalt-related (Salr) as a brake on mTORC1-driven growth and fat storage. Salr responds to the integrated stress response, a different cue from the one that activates FoxO, and the two act in a convergent way. PubMed lists Hietakangas at the University of Helsinki.

highlights.DEN2026: Last author of the study identifying Salr as an integrated-stress-response-driven brake on mTORC1 growth in Drosophila.

Pirscoveanu DF.lab_name: Department of Neurology, University of Medicine and Pharmacy Craiova (Craiova, Romania)
Pirscoveanu DF.role: First author of a 2026 review on why lifespan extension through pathways such as mTOR works less well in mammals.
Pirscoveanu DF.sub: Department of Neurology, University of Medicine and Pharmacy Craiova, Romania
story: Denisa Pirscoveanu was first author of a 2026 review article. It argues that treatments aimed at ageing pathways such as mTOR/TOR extend lifespan a lot in simple organisms like worms and flies, but much less in mammals. The authors point to many tissues sharing control, built-in redundancy and drug-handling complexity as reasons. As a review, it does not report new experiments. PubMed lists Pirscoveanu at the University of Medicine and Pharmacy Craiova.

highlights.PIR2026: First author of the review proposing that lifespan gains shrink in mammals because of system-level buffering.

Popa-Wagner A.lab_name: Department of Neurology, University of Medicine and Pharmacy Craiova (Craiova, Romania)
Popa-Wagner A.role: Senior (last) author of a 2026 review on why lifespan extension through pathways such as mTOR works less well in mammals.
Popa-Wagner A.sub: Department of Neurology, University of Medicine and Pharmacy Craiova, Romania
story: Aurel Popa-Wagner was last author of a 2026 review on the limits of lifespan extension. It describes how mTOR/TOR interventions give large gains in simple organisms but smaller ones in mammals, where ageing is spread across many tissues with backup systems and complex drug behaviour. It is a review, so it gathers earlier results rather than adding new data. PubMed lists Popa-Wagner at the University of Medicine and Pharmacy Craiova.

highlights.PIR2026: Last author of the review proposing that lifespan gains shrink in mammals because of system-level buffering.

Song H.lab_name: Department of Biomedical Science and Engineering, Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology (Gwangju, South Korea)
Song H.role: First author of a 2026 mouse study of urolithin A, mitophagy and the AMPK-mTOR axis in HFpEF.
Song H.sub: Department of Biomedical Science and Engineering, Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology, South Korea
story: Hangyul Song was first author of a 2026 study in mice with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Urolithin A, a compound made by gut bacteria, eased heart stiffness, enlargement and scarring. It switched on AMPK and lowered mTOR activity, which restored mitophagy, the clearing of damaged mitochondria, and it also changed the gut microbiome-ceramide link. The data are from mice and cells. PubMed lists Song at the Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology.

highlights.SONH2026: First author of the study showing that urolithin A improves HFpEF in mice through AMPK-mTOR-controlled mitophagy.

Oh CM.lab_name: Department of Biomedical Science and Engineering, Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology (Gwangju, South Korea)
Oh CM.role: Senior (last) author of a 2026 mouse study of urolithin A, mitophagy and the AMPK-mTOR axis in HFpEF.
Oh CM.sub: Department of Biomedical Science and Engineering, Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology, South Korea
story: Chang-Myung Oh was last author of a 2026 study in mice with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Urolithin A improved heart function and structure by activating AMPK, lowering mTOR activity and restoring mitophagy, and it reduced circulating ceramides through changes in the gut microbiome. The findings come from mice and cell models. PubMed lists Oh at the Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology.

highlights.SONH2026: Last author of the study showing that urolithin A improves HFpEF in mice through AMPK-mTOR-controlled mitophagy.

Mugale MN.lab_name: Division of Toxicology and Experimental Medicine, CSIR-Central Drug Research Institute (Lucknow, India)
Mugale MN.role: Senior (last) author of a 2026 rat study on testosterone, autophagy and mTOR in liver fibrosis.
Mugale MN.sub: Division of Toxicology and Experimental Medicine, CSIR-Central Drug Research Institute, Lucknow, India
story: Madhav Nilakhanth Mugale was last author of a 2026 study in rats with liver fibrosis caused by carbon tetrachloride. Testosterone propionate kept autophagy and mitochondria working, partly by sustaining mTOR activity, while castration made the damage worse. The work used rats and cell assays, not people. PubMed lists Mugale at the CSIR-Central Drug Research Institute in Lucknow.

highlights.VER2026: Last author of the study linking testosterone to preserved autophagic flux and mTOR signalling in rat liver fibrosis.

Zhu L.lab_name: Department of Occupational Health and Environmental Health, School of Public Health, Anhui Medical University (Hefei, China)
Zhu L.role: First author of a 2026 mouse study on LKB1/AMPK, mTOR-dependent mitophagy and liver injury after trichloroethylene exposure.
Zhu L.sub: Department of Occupational Health and Environmental Health, School of Public Health, Anhui Medical University, China
story: Lifu Zhu was first author of a 2026 mouse study on liver injury in animals sensitized to trichloroethylene, an industrial solvent. Loss of LKB1/AMPK signalling disturbed mTOR-controlled mitophagy, so damaged mitochondria leaked DNA into the cell and inflamed the liver. Rapamycin and AMPK activation protected the animals. There were no human data. PubMed lists Zhu at Anhui Medical University.

highlights.ZHU2026: First author of the study linking LKB1/AMPK loss to mTOR-dependent mitophagy failure and liver injury in mice.

Jibrin W.role: First author of a 2026 cell-line study testing whether rapamycin protects spermatogonial cells from cisplatin.
Jibrin W.sub: School of Medicine, University of Dundee, UK
story: Wafiya Jibrin was first author of a 2026 cell-culture study. It tested whether rapamycin could protect a mouse sperm-precursor cell line (GC6-spg) from damage by the cancer drug cisplatin. It did not, unlike reports in female fertility models. The work was done in vitro only. PubMed lists Jibrin at the University of Dundee.

highlights.JIB2026: First author of the study finding that rapamycin did not protect a spermatogonial cell line from cisplatin.

Lopes F.role: Senior (last) author of a 2026 cell-line study testing whether rapamycin protects spermatogonial cells from cisplatin.
Lopes F.sub: School of Medicine, University of Dundee, UK
story: Federica Lopes was last author of a 2026 cell-culture study on protecting male fertility during cancer treatment. Rapamycin did not shield a mouse sperm-precursor cell line from cisplatin damage, unlike reports in female fertility models. The work was in vitro only. PubMed lists Lopes at the University of Dundee.

highlights.JIB2026: Last author of the study finding that rapamycin did not protect a spermatogonial cell line from cisplatin.
